title: A Leader in Data Integration—six years running
author: FaisalMohamood

content.text:
Microsoft is a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Data Integration Tools
For the sixth consecutive year, Microsoft has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Data Integration Tools—and this year, the story isn't just about unifying data, it's about what customers are building on it. In our view, it reflects how far Microsoft Fabric has come—from a unified platform to an open, AI-ready foundation that connects data across clouds, formats, and partners.
Gartner evaluates vendors on two critical dimensions: Completeness of Vision and Ability to Execute. Microsoft offers Microsoft Fabric, Azure Data Factory, SQL Server Data Integration Services (SSIS), Power Query, and Azure Synapse Analytics as its data integration tools. The report noted Microsoft’s global reach, industry diversity and our ongoing investment in innovative data integration capabilities. The MQ measures both the strength of the vision as well as ability to execute. The 2026 iteration firmly places Microsoft as a leader. We agree with Gartner’s perspective that our success hinges on delivering seamless integration across Microsoft’s Data Integration portfolio, unifying experiences across data sources, and building a strong, engaged community that drives adoption and advocacy.
The report also observed that with a broad global presence serving customers across industries, we continue to invest in advancing Fabric’s data integration capabilities, including real-time data, AI enablement, and data governance, helping organizations unlock greater value from their data.
Figure: Magic Quadrant for Data Integration Tools
Our key strengths
Unified vision for data management: Microsoft Fabric brings together data integration and data management in a unified platform, empowering both technical and business users to build, manage, and deliver end-to-end data pipelines. This includes support for diverse data integration scenarios and AI-driven workloads, simplifying how organizations turn data into value.
Open ecosystem and interoperability: We continue to expand Fabric’s interoperability capabilities, making it easier for customers to connect, integrate, and work with data wherever it lives. From expanding Mirroring and OneLake shortcuts to integrating with Apache Spark and Apache Airflow, and partnering with dbt for native transformations, we are committed to providing customers with flexibility and choice.
Thriving community and partner ecosystem: Our growing global partner ecosystem and Fabric community are critical to accelerating customer success. Through investments in partner enablement, systems integrator expertise, and global events and conferences, we are expanding access to the skills, resources, and support customers need to realize the full potential of Microsoft’s Data Integration portfolio.
In addition, with the breadth and depth of today’s data estate, governance is critical. Capabilities like data lineage, policy enforcements, observability and monitoring give customers the confidence to deploy widely while having the insights they need to monitor, control and optimize. Additionally, the ever-growing range of data sources available with mirroring and shortcuts enable customers to harmonize their multi-cloud and hybrid data estates in OneLake to enable our customers’ frontier transformation ambitions. We believe the entirety of these product truths reflect the priorities our customers have asked for: one platform for every data professional, openness across clouds and formats, deep insights to govern effectively and a thriving ecosystem to help them succeed.
Microsoft Fabric: your unified, AI-powered data estate
At the core of our data integration strategy is Microsoft Fabric, a unified, AI-powered data and analytics platform designed to simplify the complexities of modern data ecosystems. Now with over 44,000 customers, Fabric delivers an all-in-one, software-as-a-service (SaaS) experience that spans data ingestion, engineering, science, real-time intelligence, and visualization—all built on Microsoft OneLake, a single, unified data lake for your entire organization.
With OneLake, you load your data once and use that single copy across every Fabric workload and engine, eliminating duplication and reducing complexity. Built on open standards such as Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg, OneLake lets Delta tables be accessed as Iceberg without data movement or conversion, while the OneLake catalog provides a central hub for data discovery, governance, and collaboration.
Many ways to bring data into OneLake
Fabric Data Factory
Fabric Data Factory integrates seamlessly with OneLake, offering cloud-scale services for data movement, orchestration, transformation, deployment, and monitoring. With native dbt support and Apache Airflow integration, data teams can use the tools they already know to tackle even the most complex ETL scenarios. Customers with existing SSIS investments can retain those workloads while modernizing with Fabric, and the on-premises data gateway connects Fabric to data behind private networks.
Shortcuts and mirroring
Shortcuts and mirroring offer a zero-copy, zero-ETL approach to bringing data into OneLake. Shortcuts virtualize data from across clouds—including Amazon S3 and Google Cloud Storage—directly into OneLake, enabling near real-time analysis through live connections to the source. Mirroring replicates operational databases and data warehouses, including Google BigQuery, into the lake, keeping data synchronized and ready for analytics. Partnerships with Snowflake, Databricks, and SAP extend bidirectional data sharing even further.
Real-Time Intelligence
Fabric Real-Time Intelligence empowers organizations to ingest and process streaming and high-granularity data instantly, driving real-time insights and automated decision-making for scenarios such as IoT analytics, fraud detection, and operational dashboards.
Whether through batch processing, incremental updates, or real-time streaming, Fabric gives organizations a secure, scalable foundation for every data integration pattern—across cloud, multicloud, and hybrid environments.
Customer success
Real customer experiences show how Microsoft Fabric is making a measurable difference. Organizations like IWG, Mercedes Benz, Mediterranean Shipping Company, LSEG, and EY have adopted Microsoft Fabric to build the robust data foundation required for AI. At IWG, shortcuts in OneLake replaced costly pipelines and data movement, helping cut report generation time by 90% and giving 2,000 users access to data insights.
"Microsoft Fabric was a game changer because of its ability to create shortcuts without physically moving data from one place to another. Before, if I had to incorporate three sources, I had to create pipelines to bring in the data. That pipeline had a cost. The data movement had a cost. With Fabric, it's two clicks and that's it."
— José Viegas, Senior Data Architect, IWG
Looking ahead
Six years in, the conversation has shifted from bringing data together to putting it to work. This year's recognition we feel reflects that shift: an open platform that meets data wherever it lives, a growing community of partners and experts, and customers like IWG turning faster access to data into real business results. We're grateful to the customers, partners, and Fabric community who help shape what we build.

• Learn more about Data Factory in Microsoft Fabric
• Learn more about Microsoft OneLake.
• Get started with Microsoft Fabric
